title: Cognizant Splits 68,000 Staff Into Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini Units
summary: Cognizant restructured 68,000 employees into three AI-specific units for Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini. Here's what the platform war looks like from inside a $5.7B IT services company.
body_markdown:
Enterprise AI Strategy


# Cognizant Splits 68,000 Staff Into Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini Units


By OpenTools Team


·


November 12, 2026


Cognizant has created three dedicated delivery units aligned to Anthropic's Claude (25,000+ staff), OpenAI (25,000+), and Google's Gemini (18,000+), all announced within 22 days. The IT services giant is betting that deep specialization plus managed services will win enterprise AI deployment contracts.


## Three Platform-Specific Armies, Announced in Three Weeks


[Cognizant](https://opentools.ai/organizations/cognizant) just did something no other IT services company has done at this scale: it carved its workforce into three distinct armies, each loyal to a different AI platform.


In the span of 22 days, the $5.7 billion IT services giant announced dedicated delivery units for **[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's Claude** (25,000+ staff, November 11), **[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai)** (25,000+, October 30), and **Google's Gemini** (18,000+, October 19), as[Channel Dive](https://www.channeldive.com/news/cognizant-splits-68000-staff-into-claude-openai-and-gemini-units/874419/) first reported. Together, the three groups hold more than 68,000 professionals — nearly a fifth of Cognizant's 359,900 employees.


The groups are **distinct and non-overlapping** . Each associate is assigned to only one AI unit at a time, though they can move between groups as skills and certifications change.


## What Each Unit Does


- **Claude Frontier Capability Group** 25,000+ staff announced November 11. About 80% are already using Claude in client work. Includes a managed services offering bundling staff, Claude licenses, and Cognizant's own AI Delivery Operating System.


- **OpenAI Frontier Capability Group** 25,000+ staff announced October 30. Focuses on **Codex for software engineering** , legacy system modernization, and deploying AI agents in sales and customer service. Over 21,000 employees have earned 40,000+ OpenAI training badges, per[TNW](https://thenextweb.com/news/cognizant-openai-frontier-capability-group-25000) .


- **Gemini Frontier Capability Group** 18,000+ staff announced October 19. Houses Frontier Certified Engineers focused on building and deploying Gemini agents. Cognizant has already trained 55,000 associates on Google's Build with Gemini program and aims for 200,000 by year-end, per[CIO Dive](https://www.ciodive.com/news/cognizant-google-cloud-gemini-ai-forward-deployed-engineers/833647/) .


## The Managed Services Play: Claude-as-a-Service


The Claude unit introduced something new: a **managed services model** that bundles dedicated staff, licensed Claude access, and[Cognizant](https://opentools.ai/organizations/cognizant) 's proprietary AI Delivery Operating System into a single contract. The pitch is predictable[AI spend](https://opentools.ai/tools/ai-spend) — clients pay one price and Cognizant owns Claude in production, licenses and all.


This is the classic MSP playbook applied to a frontier model. As[Channel Dive](https://www.channeldive.com/news/cognizant-splits-68000-staff-into-claude-openai-and-gemini-units/874419/) reports, Paul Smith,[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's Chief Commercial Officer, framed the talent crunch directly: "The people with the skills to make it work inside a real business have become the hardest talent to find."


The initial focus areas are redesigning business domains around AI, modernizing underlying systems, operating agents securely at scale, and engineering AI-native software.


## The Numbers Behind the Strategy


CEO Ravi Kumar S told analysts on the October 29 earnings call that[Cognizant](https://opentools.ai/organizations/cognizant) now has "a lot of deals bundling[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's Claude,[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's Codex, and Cognizant's own inference units along with services." In high-volume workflows, he said, clients "no longer want to buy software and services separately."


The bundling strategy helped lift Q3 revenue 4.8% in constant currency to $5.7 billion,[per Channel Dive](https://www.channeldive.com/news/cognizant-splits-68000-staff-into-claude-openai-and-gemini-units/874419/) . But CFO Jatin Dalal cautioned that Q4 will see a slightly lower contribution from resales, and the full-year growth outlook was trimmed to 4%-4.4%.


## The Platform War Arrives in the Enterprise


[Cognizant](https://opentools.ai/organizations/cognizant) is explicitly not betting on a single model provider. By creating three parallel units — each with its own leadership, training pipeline, and client engagement model — the company is positioning itself as the Switzerland of enterprise AI deployment. Whatever platform a client picks, Cognizant has an army ready.


[Accenture](https://opentools.ai/organizations/accenture) made a similar move last December with a ~30,000-person Claude training group. But Cognizant's three-platform approach is more aggressive — it's essentially running a multi-model experiment at the scale of a Fortune 500 company.


Omdia Chief Analyst Alastair Edwards told[Channel Dive](https://www.channeldive.com/news/cognizant-splits-68000-staff-into-claude-openai-and-gemini-units/874419/) that he expects power to tilt toward partners within 12-18 months as AI vendors lean on deployment skills they don't have in-house. But Gartner warns buyers to watch for providers that rebrand traditional consulting as specialized AI deployment and charge a premium for it.


## What This Means for AI Builders


If you're a developer or engineer working in enterprise AI,[Cognizant](https://opentools.ai/organizations/cognizant) 's restructure is a signal about where the jobs are going:


**Platform specialization is becoming a career path.** Cognizant's Frontier Certified Engineers are explicitly positioned as "model-agnostic builders" — people who can work across Claude, Codex, and Gemini. The fastest-growing job designation in tech right now is the Forward Deployed Engineer, with postings surging from under 200 in 2023 to over 7,300 in the first nine months of 2026, per[CIO Dive](https://www.ciodive.com/news/cognizant-google-cloud-gemini-ai-forward-deployed-engineers/833647/) citing Lightcast data.


**The talent bottleneck is real and deepening.** Only a couple thousand practicing FDEs exist, creating fierce competition. AWS funneled $1 billion into an FDE business unit.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) acquired Northslope, an enterprise deployment company. Cognizant is betting that owning the deployment layer — not just consulting on it — is where the margin lives.
